video_title: Can Knicks Win the Title?  + What Lottery Reform Means for Tanking | ALL NBA PODCAST

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' impressive playoff run and their status as underdogs
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks are going to be the underdog in the finals

text_blocks.speaker: Adam Mares
text_blocks.text: Do you think that matters? The finals you get a nice break anyway, but they will have an extended break if they are able to close this out in four.

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Stein
text_blocks.text: I think it matters. The Knicks are going to be the underdog in the finals and yes, we are going to take the leap and say that they are not going to be the first team in league history to blow a 3-0 lead. It helps them, OG Anunoby is still working his way back. Why not? If you are the Knicks, you would welcome it, you would take it.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' historic playoff performance and their championship potential
quotes.excerpt: This really is their best chance in more than 30 years
quotes.quote: The Knicks have not been to the NBA finals this century. They have since two one-point losses in a row to Atlanta. They have been rolling, a monster, 10 wins in a row, the scoring margin is significant. So the Knicks getting back on that stage for the first time since 1999, and of course, they were injury-compromised in 1999. This really is their best chance in more than 30 years since the 94 finals that went seven with Houston. It is going to be a momentous finals. We are either going to get the Knicks' first championship in more than 50 years, or Victor Wembanyama's first championship, or the first repeat champion we have seen with the Thunder since the dynastic Warriors in 2017 and 2018. One way or another, the champion this season, it is going to be a huge deal, great significance, and there will be lots of eyeballs on it.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown's journey as the sixth choice for the Knicks' coaching job
quotes.excerpt: Mike Brown at best was the sixth choice for this job
quotes.quote: Mike Brown at best was the sixth choice for this job. Remember that the Knicks asked for permission to speak to Jason Kidd, Ime Udoka, Quinn Snyder, Chris Finch, and Billy Donovan. All of those teams said no. Jason Kidd and Billy Donovan both got contract extensions and no longer coach the teams where they were a year ago. It really looked like the Knicks fired Tom Thibodeau without a plan to replace the first coach who had taken them to the conference finals this century. For things to turn around to this degree, the teamwork, the way that team has come together, the way Karl-Anthony Towns has embraced a new role, the way Mikal Bridges, who has been so maligned for how many draft picks he cost the Knicks, and the level that he has been playing in these playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: The Cavaliers' difficult offseason decisions after their playoff loss
quotes.excerpt: They are looking at nothing but difficult decisions
quotes.quote: They are in that club with Minnesota and Denver. They are looking at nothing but difficult decisions. They lost this series after Game 1. Normally in the NBA, the outside world, all of us in the basketball public, when you see a team blow a game like that, 22-point lead on the road, a chance to steal Game 1, we overreact and we say they will never recover. And frequently in the NBA, teams actually do recover or make somewhat of a recovery from a loss like that. The Cavaliers have not. The Cavaliers blew that game and very predictably, they have looked awful since then. Donovan Mitchell is contract extension eligible on July 7th. We talk so much about Giannis Antetokounmpo, Giannis is not contract extension eligible until October 1st. Donovan Mitchell, contract extension eligible on July 7th. Will he extend? If he will not extend, do the Cavaliers have to feel trade offers for Donovan Mitchell? Even if the Donovan Mitchell situation resolves itself, can Kenny Atkinson come back as coach after a conference finals like this? What is the move Cleveland is going to make to get themselves out of the second apron? Will this finally be the offseason that they trade Jared Allen? And then James Harden. The assumption was he would not have pushed for a trade from the Clippers to the Cavaliers at the February deadline if he was not confident in the extreme that he was going to get a multi-year contract extension, rather than wait to see how the Clippers were going to handle the team option on his deal. And Evan Mobley. We know they do not want to trade him, but what if that is their best move? Would they use Mobley to try to get into the Giannis sweepstakes? The Cavaliers are as fascinating a team because of all these questions about their future as any team you want to pick.

quotes.speaker: Mark Stein
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of the new lottery reform on team trade strategies
quotes.excerpt: The more we learn about this proposal, there is only two things I like
quotes.quote: The more we learn about this proposal, there is only two things I like, Adam Mares. One of them is the relegation zone. I do take my hat off to the league that even though it is not relegation like in European soccer that you know I love, but the NBA with the draft relegation zone is poised to become the first league that has found a way to just work relegation into its lexicon somehow, and fans will like that. So that, that I am good with. And what that means is the teams with the three worst records next season will only have a 5.4% shot at number one as opposed to 8.1%, and the implication is that the teams in the bottom three are going to be trying desperately at the end of the season to get out of the bottom three. I do like that. The only other thing I like though is that this new proposal is only going to be three years.
